title: Anonymization rules for a project
description: Goal, suitability, file rules and what to keep, generalize and remove in one project. Must not hold personal data about the people interviewed or mentioned.

policy_version.description: Version of the rules. Changed when the rules change, and written in every change list.

goal.description: anonymous = the data may be used by providers without a data processing agreement; requires deleting the keys. risk_reduction = the keys are kept, and the data is still processed as personal data at approved providers.

assessment.description: The suitability decision, made by a human before the data is read.

recipients.description: Who will use the anonymized data, and what do they know about the population? For example whether they know the list of respondents.

suitable.description: Can the data be responsibly anonymized without losing its purpose?

keys.description: Keys outside the project folder to delete when the goal is anonymous, for example data in the collection tool, recruitment lists and backups. raw/, changes/ and review/ come in addition.

decided_by.description: Who made the decision. A role is enough.

population.description: Who the respondents are, how many, and how well they and the readers know each other. The smaller and better known the population, the stricter the assessment.

analysis_needs.description: What the analysis needs to keep, for example size of municipality or type of role.

keep.description: What may stay unchanged, for example the names of tools or public schemes that the study is about.

generalize.description: Identifiers replaced by a more general description.

remove.description: What is always removed and marked.

placeholders.description: Pattern for placeholders per category. n is numbered per document (per row in CSV files, per record in JSON Lines files).

files.description: File rules. The first rule whose match pattern fits the path under raw/ applies. Files without a rule are handled by their extension; CSV and JSON Lines files need a rule.

match.description: Pattern for the path under raw/, for example data/*.csv. * matches any characters, also /.

action.description: anonymize (default), copy unchanged (only files without personal data) or exclude.

type.description: By default from the file extension.

note.description: Why the rule is as it is.

keep_columns.description: CSV: kept unchanged, for example fixed answer options that do not identify.

date_columns.description: CSV: timestamps shortened to the date.

drop_columns.description: CSV: removed, for example respondent ID, email and municipality.

name_columns.description: CSV: columns whose values are names. The residual check searches the output for them.

id.description: JSON Lines: path to the record ID. It is replaced with a new ID. Without it, the line number is used.

text.description: JSON Lines: paths to free text to anonymize, for example messages[].content.

keep.description: JSON Lines: paths kept unchanged, for example messages[].role.

dates.description: JSON Lines: paths to timestamps shortened to the date.

names.description: JSON Lines: paths whose values are names. The residual check searches the output for them.

skip.description: JSON Lines: records with all of these values are left out, for example {"is_test": true}.
